summary.title: gitlet.js
summary.one_liner: Read a commented JavaScript implementation of Git's core commands (init, add, commit, branch, checkout, fetch, merge, push, clone) to see how Git works internally.
takeaways: Git in six hundred words: a plain-English walkthrough of init, add, commit, clone, pull, branch, checkout and push using a two-repository example.
How Git stores content: add creates blob objects and updates the index; commit creates tree and commit objects and moves the branch pointer.
How fetch records a remote branch and writes FETCH_HEAD, and how pull then runs a merge that can be a fast-forward.
The gitlet.js source is heavily commented and shows how each command checks preconditions (e.g., dirty working copy, non-bare repo, conflicts) before acting.
summary.summary: The page is the annotated source of gitlet.js, a small Git clone written in JavaScript for Node.js, intended to be readable and heavily commented. It opens with "Git in six hundred words", a narrative that walks through init, add, commit, clone, pull, branch, checkout and push between two local repositories. The main body then implements each API function (init, add, rm, commit, branch, checkout, diff, remote, fetch, merge, pull, push, status, clone), with comments explaining the steps and the error cases. The page links to a longer deep dive, "Git from the inside out", for more detail.
